definition: RDKB Core is a collection of foundational building-blocks called "components." They're designed for easier reuse, improved modularity, RDK Ready vendor certification, reduced code size, and consistent interface definitions.

goals.title: Easier Component Reuse
goals.goal: Core RDKB components must be easy to reuse across every device profile — from a simple modem/ONU, to an Ethernet router or Wi-Fi gateway, to an EasyMesh controller or extender, to add-on profiles like app lifecycle management and IoT.
goals.challenge: Historical releases focused narrowly on the Ethernet Wi-Fi Router or Wi-Fi Gateway profile, so code carried assumptions that made reuse difficult elsewhere — operators had to modify components themselves, increasing time-to-market and cost.

goals.title: Modularity — Build-Time Dependencies
goals.goal: Avoid tight coupling and unnecessary build-time dependencies. Developers shouldn't have to manually edit and strip dependencies every time a component is reused.
goals.challenge: Some components have problem build-time dependencies with other components. If these components are not in the software build, then a build time error will occur. For example: OneWifi, WAN Manager, DHCP Manager, P&M, Utopia, Test and Diag, TR-069 PA, Xconf, and others — carry an unnecessary build-time dependency on the cable modem HAL interface today.

goals.title: Modularity — Run-Time Dependencies
goals.goal: Run-time dependencies to optional components and apps must be flexible and dynamic. A component that relies on another's methods or properties must keep providing its expected feature subset even when that component isn't present.
goals.challenge: Some components have problem run-time dependencies with other components. If these components are not in the software build, then a run-time error, unexpected behavior or crash may occur. For example: Utopia, RFC, CcspCr, Test and Diag, TR-069 PA, Xconf, OneWifi, CcspWiFiAgent, CcspHotspot, and others — have an inflexible run-time dependency on T2 telemetry. This can be a problem because T2 telemetry is an optional component; some operators use other telemetry approaches entirely.

goals.title: Reduced Code Size
goals.goal: Code must scale from small modem/ONUs and extenders up to high-end gateways with apps and IoT. Each component should support a limited, well-defined feature set, allocate only the memory it needs, and be easy to exclude when not needed.
goals.challenge: Large components like Utopia and P&M are hard to reason about or extract from the build. Some code (e.g. CCSP Common Lib) over-allocates memory, and documentation on including/excluding optional components needs improvement.

goals.title: Consistent Interface Definitions
goals.goal: Use a common way to persist values and a standard IPC mechanism between components, with test code that exercises that IPC the way it's actually used in production — a pre-validated core reduces integration and testing cycles.
goals.challenge: Multiple persistence approaches are in use today (sysConfig, PSM, Platform HAL, mySQL), and some older components still use SysEvent, DMCLI, or Common Lib for IPC instead of RBUS.

rdk_ready.title: Well-defined interfaces to vendor code
rdk_ready.body: Use industry-standard vendor interfaces (e.g. NL80211) as the RDKB HAL wherever they already exist. Where gaps remain, RDK components support an RDK-defined HAL interface — or a standard HAL interface plus RDK-defined HAL extensions. Vendor interfaces evolve over time, so tight version control is maintained between each HAL spec, the RDKB component using it, and the vendor code certified against it.

rdk_ready.title: Test and certification program
rdk_ready.body: A test mechanism exists for each individual HAL interface spec, and every vendor runs the same tests. A formal certification process verifies vendor compliance with specific HAL interfaces and versions. Because certification is modular, a Wi-Fi SoC vendor certifies only against the RDKB Wi-Fi HAL and a DOCSIS SoC vendor only against the Cable Modem HAL — so operators can mix and match vendors (e.g. Wi-Fi from Vendor A, GPON from Vendor B) on the same platform.

items: Code size that scales across device types
Test code provided for each HAL interface

value_proposition: RDKB core enables easier code reuse, faster development, and consistent behavior across diverse vendors and device types.
